findings.title: The owner pre-correction gate omits mandatory concurrence roles for the selected stop classes
findings.evidence: The owner resolution names only fresh Full-contract and Lite-conformance concurrence before product correction. The exact proposal it cites requires, at the same pre-implementer order, fresh migration, fresh security, and independent authority/concurrency concurrence in addition to that pair. The owner-selected rules alter bootstrap/migration staging, abort states and generation/session invalidation, credential rotation, collision/redaction, and final-gate race winners. The ratified governance matrix assigns those stop classes to the omitted roles and says repair starts only after every required verdict accepts.
findings.impact: The exact authorization bytes conflict on who must concur before successor-F1 correction. Treating the two-role field as exhaustive would bypass ratified stop authority; treating the longer sequence as controlling contradicts the owner-resolution gate. Product correction cannot begin.
findings.required_resolution: Issue a replacement owner-resolution artifact at a new hash that explicitly preserves the serial mandatory migration, security, and authority/concurrency concurrence mini-waves, in addition to Full-contract and Lite-conformance concurrence, before any successor-F1 product correction.

findings.title: R07 cursor restart success contradicts the ratified process-memory reference lifecycle
findings.evidence: R07 says an unexpired valid cursor resumes from SQLite after process restart and claims public page semantics are unchanged. Ratified D0 makes record_ref and scope_ref resolver mappings process-memory-only and invalidates every reference on process restart. The public lineage, graph, navigation-discover continuation, and navigation-audit operations require caller-supplied live same-session references and private resolution/physical requalification; graph.temporal.read always requires a live non-null scope_ref, and navigation.discover rejects null scope with a continuation cursor. Persisting only redacted page payload and reference digests cannot perform the required live resolve/physical requalification after the resolver is gone.
findings.impact: The correction must either reject these cursor continuations after restart, contrary to R07, or create a new durable reference/requalification authority or continuation exception, changing ratified public success semantics and security dependencies. No operation-specific restart rule resolves this conflict.
findings.required_resolution: Obtain an explicit owner semantic choice and required MCP/security concurrence: either make cursor invalidation after restart normative for reference-bound public tools, or define a closed, count-preserving continuation protocol that does not persist raw paths, does not add a record/table/operation, preserves current authorization and physical requalification, and explicitly acknowledges any public-success semantic effect.

findings.title: The exact-looking 18-vector preservation field is not reconciled with mandatory per-scenario negative families
findings.evidence: R06 freezes a subtotal of 8 existing core-operation vectors plus 10 restore/bootstrap recovery vectors, while the owner resolution labels 18 as non_mcp_core_vectors without saying subtotal/minimum. DC06 simultaneously requires every scenario to be a separate closed executable case, and the prior accepted reviews require many additional anchor, collision, non-enumeration, global-event, reference, cursor, policy, rate, retention, redaction, backup, timestamp, and race cases. ANCHOR-INTENT-001 through 009 alone consumes nine cases beyond the named 8+10 class. The proposal does not supply an exhaustive replacement_fixture_ids ledger or a count rule for these additional cases.
findings.impact: An implementer can preserve 18 only by collapsing or omitting mandatory scenarios, or can materialize the required cases and violate an apparent exact preservation target. Fixture counts, generated hashes, manifest bytes, and evidence assertions are indeterminate.
findings.required_resolution: Amend the owner-resolution/correction map to state that 18 is only the exact 8+10 named-class subtotal, freeze the additional executable-family accounting and replacement fixture IDs, and state the resulting fixture/count/hash consequences while preserving the 67 official MCP IDs.

findings.title: R15 selects a collision guard without defining its cryptographic contract
findings.evidence: R15 distinguishes a subject_digest collision by comparing a distinct authenticated canonical-subject collision guard/evidence digest, and says external_mapping gains or binds such a digest. R12 also calls authenticated_by a closed adapter identifier/evidence digest. Neither rule freezes the field name and separation, digest algorithm, domain separator, canonical preimage, versioning, equality rule, adapter-evidence binding, or how an authenticated adapter proves two distinct canonical subjects while raw subjects remain forbidden. Mapping remains unavailable until a separately ratified adapter, but R15 nevertheless requires exact collision vectors and a deterministic error distinction in the successor pack.
findings.impact: The selected 53-code outcome is clear, but the predicate selecting IDENTITY_COLLISION versus MAPPING_CONFLICT is not machine-exact or independently testable. Implementations can invent incompatible guard constructions or cannot inject the required subject-digest collision at all.
findings.required_resolution: Freeze a closed, versioned authenticated mapping evidence record and an independent collision-guard digest field with exact algorithm/domain/preimage/canonicalization/equality rules, or explicitly defer subject-digest collision qualification to the separately ratified adapter contract and adjust successor-F1 vectors without weakening one-shot/no-mutation collision behavior.

findings.title: The owner resolution does not unambiguously adopt DC01 through DC13 as normative correction bytes
findings.evidence: The proposal explicitly requires the owner to ratify the derived corrections as one bounded correction record. The owner statement says ratify all 15 D0-15 recommendations, and owner_selections enumerates only R01 through R15. The resolution references the proposal hash and reports derived_corrections=13, but it contains no normative adoption statement or ID list for DC01 through DC13. A count/reference alone does not say whether those rules are adopted authority or merely proposal metadata.
findings.impact: DC01 through DC13 carry essential error, stale-state, policy, rate, schema, vector, timestamp, backup, credential, event, binding, retention, and regeneration obligations. Successor-F1 correction cannot rely on them without inferring owner authority.
findings.required_resolution: Replace or amend the owner resolution with an explicit hash-bound normative adoption of D015-DC01 through D015-DC13, subject to correction of FFC-D015-002 through FFC-D015-004.
